oneTimers: Share-based pay is the main gap between the two profit numbers: the non-GAAP reconciliation adds back $343M of equity-settled share-based compensation plus $90M of related employer taxes (net of R&D incentives) and $7M of disposal and restructuring costs, which is why GAAP net income of $270M sits far below non-GAAP net income of $480M.

Net income got a $128M lift from income on equity investments — mostly $126M of fair-value gains on shares in publicly listed companies. That is market-driven, not operating profit, and Arm excludes it from its non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Combined other income was $162M: interest income of $31M plus $3M of other non-operating income (together the $34M shown as other income), plus $128M of income from equity investments — mostly fair-value gains on shares in listed companies. Tax was a $17M benefit, not a charge.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 23% YoY on continued strong demand, several high-value license agreements, and contributions from backlog.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 22% YoY on higher royalty rates from newer designs such as Armv9 and Arm CSS, with data center royalties more than doubling.

sources.label: Official earnings release — shareholder letter, Form 6-K Exhibit 99.2 (SEC EDGAR)
Quarterly report with financial statements, Form 6-K (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: License revenue rose 23% to $574M and royalty revenue 22% to $715M — a record first quarter. Data center royalties more than doubled as Arm-based server chips spread, and Neoverse shipments have now passed 1.5 billion cores.
takeaways.title: Both halves of the business grew over 20%

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.25 while non-GAAP EPS was $0.45. The gap is mostly $343M of share-based pay plus $90M of employer taxes — and $128M of net income came from fair-value gains on listed-company investments, not operations.
takeaways.title: GAAP profit is much smaller than the headline

takeaways.text: Arm guided Q2 FY27 revenue to $1.38B (plus or minus $50M) with non-GAAP EPS of $0.47 (plus or minus $0.04). Demand for its new Arm AGI CPU now exceeds $2B across fiscal 2027–28, double the $1B opportunity outlined last quarter.
takeaways.title: Next quarter is guided higher

verdict: Arm's revenue hit a record $1.29B, up 22%, with data center royalties more than doubling — but GAAP profit stayed thin at $270M, and nearly half of it came from gains on investments, not the chip business.
